item.title: 'Very disappointed with Vladimir': Trump criticises Putin for continuing Ukraine war
item.description: US President Donald Trump expressed disappointment with Russian President Vladimir Putin over the ongoing war in Ukraine, calling it the most significant event since World War II in terms of casualties. Trump stated he had a good relationship with Putin and questioned why the war continues, noting its negative impact on Russia and its prolonged duration.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: AFC 2025: Qatar defeats UAE 2–1 to qualify for FIFA World Cup 2026; is this the end of UAE?
item.description: Qatar defeated the UAE 2–1 in a decisive AFC World Cup 2026 qualifier in Doha, securing their spot in next year’s tournament. Two second-half headers gave Qatar the edge, while UAE’s late goal wasn’t enough. Needing only a draw, UAE now heads to the fifth-round playoffs. The win marks Qatar’s first World Cup qualification through the standard route.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Gaza crackdown: Hamas posts video of public execution of 'collaborators and outlaws'; 4 hostages’ remains return to Israel
item.description: Hamas executed men branded collaborators amidst street clashes. A US-brokered truce is in effect. Israel confirmed the return of more hostage remains. Hamas security units are patrolling Gaza. US President Donald Trump vowed to disarm Hamas. A peace plan calls for a demilitarised Gaza. Families continue to press for the return of all hostages.

item.title: ‘Hostile act’: Trump says considering terminating business with China; threatens to end cooking oil trade
item.description: President Trump accused China of "purposefully" halting soybean purchases, labeling it an "economically hostile act." He stated the US is considering trade termination with Beijing as retribution, emphasizing domestic cooking oil production capabilities. This move follows China's previous use of trade leverage, impacting American soybean farmers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Did Israel proofread it first?’: Donald Trump's son trolled after signing books in 'empty' store
item.description: Donald Trump promoted his son Eric's new memoir "Under Siege" on Truth Social, calling it a "phenomenal book." However, a video of Eric's book signing at a Florida bookstore appeared to show an empty store, leading to social media mockery. Despite the perceived low turnout, the book reportedly climbed Amazon's best-seller chart.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘You won’t see me in bathing suit’: Trump takes another swipe at Biden; jokes about beach photos and falls
item.description: President Trump mocked Joe Biden's recent beach trip and his struggles with stairs, contrasting it with his own potential visit to Argentina. Trump claimed he would not be seen in a bathing suit on a beach or unable to lift a light chair, unlike Biden. This follows Trump's previous criticisms of Biden's public appearances.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Riyadh fashion week 2025: British icons Stella McCartney and Vivienne Westwood to headline star-studded event
item.description: Riyadh Fashion Week 2025 will feature style legends Vivienne Westwood and Stella McCartney, marking their regional debuts. The event, from October 16-21, will showcase over 30 runway shows, blending punk aesthetics with local artistry and sustainable glamour, positioning Saudi Arabia as an emerging fashion capital.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who is Ashley Tellis, Indian-origin expert in US, who came under fire for Chinese link?
item.description: Prominent Indian-origin strategist Ashley Tellis faces serious accusations of removing classified documents and meeting with Chinese officials. Authorities reportedly found over a thousand 'Top Secret' and 'Secret' documents at his residence during a raid. Prosecutors allege Tellis printed sensitive U.S. Air Force data and held discussions with Chinese representatives regarding international relations and technology.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US targets suspected drug-terror vessel off Venezuela; six killed in strike, Trump says — Watch
item.description: President Trump announced a lethal strike off the coast of Venezuela, killing six individuals on a vessel affiliated with a "Designated Terrorist Organization" allegedly involved in narcotrafficking. The strike, ordered by the Secretary of War, occurred in international waters and marks the fifth fatal operation in the Caribbean under the administration's policy of treating drug traffickers as unlawful combatants.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Four-time Grammy winner D’Angelo dies at 51 after battling cancer
item.description: R&B icon D'Angelo, born Michael Eugene Archer, has died at 51 after a battle with cancer. A pioneer of neo-soul, he released three Grammy-winning albums, including "Brown Sugar" and "Voodoo." His career was marked by innovative music and a memorable performance in the "Untitled (How Does It Feel)" video.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Phase two begins right now': Donald Trump on Gaza peace deal; demands dead hostages from Hamas
item.description: Following a hostage swap, former President Trump urged for a "phase 2" of negotiations, stating the "job is not done" as dead hostages have not been returned. Israel announced plans to cut aid to Gaza by half, citing Hamas's alleged ceasefire violations by delaying the return of deceased hostages.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Except one, other news outlets reject Pentagon’s new press rules — US media and Trump still at odds: what’s behind the rift?
item.description: Major news organizations are refusing to sign a new Pentagon policy that severely restricts journalists' access, requiring escorts and barring unapproved interactions with Defense Department personnel. The policy, criticized as an attempt to stifle a free press, only saw one outlet agree to its terms. Reporters who don't comply face badge revocation and eviction from their workspaces.

item.title: ‘Her lips move like a machine gun’: Donald Trump makes another wild remark on Karoline Leavitt — Watch
item.description: Donald Trump praised White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, highlighting her rapid rise and effectiveness. He described her speaking style as "like a machine gun," calling her a "star" and "the best press secretary anyone has ever had." Leavitt, at 28, is the youngest to hold the position and previously served as an assistant press secretary.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: AI Takes Office: Abu Dhabi unveils world’s first AI-powered public servant at GITEX Global 2025
item.description: Abu Dhabi has launched TAMM AutoGov, a groundbreaking AI public servant. This system will proactively manage government services for residents. Imagine your driving license renewing itself or bills being paid automatically. This initiative aims to make government interactions faster and more personalized. It marks a significant shift towards anticipatory governance, promising less paperwork and fewer missed deadlines for citizens.

item.title: Trump's effort in mediating Israel-Hamas ceasefire gets global attention — and even Kamala Harris- Are Democrats mending ties with US president
item.description: Former Vice President Kamala Harris publicly commended President Trump for securing the release of 20 Israeli hostages held by Hamas, calling it an "important first step toward a more hopeful future." While acknowledging the breakthrough, Harris also stressed that significant work remains to achieve lasting peace and security for both Israelis and Palestinians.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Vivek Ramaswamy wishes Charlie Kirk on his birthday as social media recalls his anti-H1B, ‘parasite’ remarks on Indians
item.description: Vivek Ramaswamy's birthday wish to the late Charlie Kirk sparked controversy due to Kirk's past anti-immigrant remarks, particularly targeting Indians. Kirk, a prominent conservative activist, was assassinated last month, with the alleged shooter citing Kirk's "hate." President Trump plans to posthumously award Kirk the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Bollywood Pickles & Gandhi Tea: Inside the crazy, wild world of desi grocery stores in UAE
item.description: Indian grocery stores in the UAE offer a unique shopping experience. They stock familiar Indian brands alongside unusual products created for the expat market. These stores provide a taste of home for millions of Indians living abroad. Frozen meals and nostalgic items cater to busy lifestyles. The stores are emotional lifelines, keeping memories alive.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
